title: Dedicated capacity: tenant-priority fallback and allocation oscillation mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple production escalations in the last two weeks exposed an oscillation mode in the reserved-pool autoscaler and the tenant-priority fallback policy. When burst demand spikes occur across tenants with similar priority, the current fallback logic aggressively reassigns burst headroom and preempts low-priority slots, triggering cascading cold-starts and transient SLO breaches. This ticket implements a short-term hotfix plus a robust algorithmic rewrite to prevent oscillation and provide predictable fallbacks for high-priority tenants.

Background: Two customers (FinHealth, AtlasCRM) reported recurrent latency spikes during peak bursts. On 2025-02-12 we saw a cluster-level thrash where repeated scale decisions oscillated allocation between tenants every ~30s window, causing allocation churn and repeated tenant preemptions. Root cause analysis indicates: (1) fallback policy favors immediate reclaim of idle headroom without dampening, (2) burst-credit accounting allowed quick re-enabled allocations with no smoothing, and (3) autoscaler decision interval and leader-election jitter amplified flips.

Goals:
- Stop allocation thrash (oscillation) under mixed-priority bursts.
- Ensure high-priority tenants retain predictable minimal headroom during incidents.
- Deploy a short-term patch to reduce customer impact, then roll out the algorithmic rewrite in runtime-1.21.

Proposed work:
1) Hotfix (immediate): introduce a 3-minute dampening window per-tenant where reclaimed headroom cannot be reallocated to the same tenant more than once within the window. Add a safety reserve (static 5% of node capacity) for tenants with SLA tagged as "priority:high". Release as hotfix-2025.02.
2) Algorithmic rewrite (medium): replace greedy fallback with a token-bucket smoothing layer and a hysteresis-based scoring model that includes: priority weight, recent allocation churn, burst-credit consumption rate, and SLO deficit. The scorer outputs a stable ordering; autoscaler enforces min-hold times per allocation.
3) Autoscaler leader election and interval tuning: extend decision reconciliation window to reduce flip sensitivity; add metrics to detect leadership jitter.
4) Observability: new dashboards showing per-tenant allocation hold-time, churn rate, and fallback events; create alert rule on >3 allocation flips within 5 minutes.

Rollout plan: hotfix -> canary on two dedicated pools (non-prod) -> quick rollout to 10% of prod pools -> 100% after 24h with no regressions. Algorithmic change to be merged after canary, feature-flagged for 2 weeks before defaulting on.

Success criteria: reduced allocation flips (<1 flip per 30m per-pool in synthetic test), customer-reported incidents resolved, and no increase in tail latency for non-priority tenants beyond acceptable levels.

Rollback plan: revert hotfix and re-enable previous fallback policy; re-run quota rebalancer to restore pre-incident allocations.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Incident opened: FinHealth escalation received at 03:12 UTC. Observed allocation flips and repeated cold starts. Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/INC-20250212-237

2025-02-13 - Initial RCA meeting. Engineering, Product, and SRE confirmed oscillation pattern; assigned to ENG-824216. Decided to implement a short dampening hotfix to stabilize production while we design the scorer model.
2025-02-18 - Ticket created and scoped by Maya. Assigned to Liam. Priority set to P0 due to customer-impacting SLO breaches.
2025-02-20 - Hotfix branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pulls/1287. Hotfix adds per-tenant 3-minute dampening + static reserve for SLA=high. Running unit + integration tests.

2025-02-22 - Canary deployed to dedicated pool: dp-west-2a-canary. Early telemetry shows allocation flips reduced from 6/min to ~0.6/min. Noticed small throughput drop for low-priority tenants (expected).

2025-02-24 - Customer comms: PM sent interim update to impacted customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full fix. Recorded customer feedback: FinHealth requests guarantee of 90th percentile latency under burst; we mapped that to priority tagging and reserve policy.

2025-02-26 - Algorithm design doc drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/priority-fallback-scorer. Proposed features: hysteresis, token-bucket smoothing, churn penalty, and min-hold duration per allocation.

2025-03-01 - Integration tests: ran synthetic burst test harness with 50 tenants. Oscillation eliminated in 95% of runs; remaining runs correlated with leader-election jitter. Added leader-election backoff adjustment to plan.
2025-03-05 - Preparing runtime-1.21 PR for algorithmic rewrite: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pulls/1315. Planning staged rollout next week.
